So the observed cycle is not a "Preisach-ordered" loop with nesting? Actually, hmm, in Preisach RPM, the down sweep order is determined by F_i− ordering and must be the reverse of the up order for the "return-point" nesting topology? Let me check the commentary text: "One can construct a history-recording device by ordering the threshold forces as F1+ < F2+ < … < FN+ and F1− > F2− > … > FN−, as sketched... Initializing in 0 state, upon increasing the force they will change states one by one in the order 1,2,…,N. Due to the choice of ordering the F_i−, this will be also the same order in which the elements return from their 1 to 0 state."

Hmm: with F1− > F2− > ... > FN−, i.e., F1 stays "1" down to the lowest force, and FN drops out first at the highest force. So on decreasing the driving force, the first element to switch back is N, then N−1... Whatever — the mathematical fact: with fixed independent thresholds and a monotone sweep, up order = increasing F+, down order = decreasing F−. No constraint linking the two orders other than within-parameter monotonicity. So the nested "loop RPM" arises automatically for independent hysterons regardless of relative orders. So the observed up/down orders differing is fine and expected for independent hysterons.
